assumptions.statement: A .safetensors filename proves the item belongs to the trusted model ecosystem, so catalog membership checks are unnecessary for such names.
assumptions.fault_name: Catalog-membership bypass via filename extension shortcut
vulnerabilities: Business-logic bypass of the model catalog membership control
Arbitrary content staging into the custom_nodes code directory

assumptions.statement: Model URLs always point at public content hosts, so no destination filtering of the outbound fetch is needed.
assumptions.fault_name: No egress allowlist on the outbound fetch

assumptions.statement: Rejecting the file:// shape as typed covers local-file schemes; case variants and authority forms do not need separate handling.
assumptions.fault_name: Scheme filter matches narrow textual forms only
vulnerabilities: Local file inclusion / arbitrary local file read

assumptions.statement: Any URL that appears in the catalog is safe to fetch, so url-by-url set membership is as strong as binding the URL to its catalog entry.
assumptions.fault_name: URL checked by catalog set membership, not bound to the admitting entry

assumptions.statement: save_path values originate from the catalog dropdown, so they are benign and need no path validation.
assumptions.fault_name: save_path accepted as an unvalidated relative path
vulnerabilities: Unrestricted remote-content write into the model store (write-what-where under models)
Path traversal via save_path (write outside the intended model subdirectory)

assumptions.statement: Clients send well-formed JSON request bodies, so parse failures cannot occur in practice.
vulnerabilities: Improper error handling on request parsing (unhandled exceptions)

assumptions.statement: ui_id is always a string produced by the manager shell, so the queue does not validate its type.
vulnerabilities: Denial of service via worker crash (serial worker starvation)

assumptions.statement: Queue counters mirror queue contents, so status readers can trust total_count and done_count as the execution truth.
assumptions.fault_name: Queue counters diverge from accepted and executed items

assumptions.statement: Only the manager shell calls start and reset, so GET semantics for state-changing operations carry no risk.
The GitHub channel is trusted to serve authentic catalog content, so catalog entries need no local integrity verification.
assumptions.fault_name: Catalog content trusted from the fixed remote channel without local integrity anchoring
vulnerabilities: Catalog poisoning leading to stored XSS in the manager shell

assumptions.statement: save_path and filename are simple names without separators, so string concatenation under the models root is safe.
assumptions.fault_name: Write path built by string concatenation without canonicalization
vulnerabilities: Archive extraction path traversal (zip-slip) on downloaded artifacts

assumptions.statement: The attributes that passed the gate are the same attributes the worker later uses.
assumptions.fault_name: Check-to-use gap between gate validation and queued attributes
vulnerabilities: Cross-entry artifact substitution (validated entry not bound to the used URL)
Supply-chain substitution via repository (HuggingFace-style repo) downloads

assumptions.statement: Each request carries a unique ui_id, so duplicate keys cannot disturb queue bookkeeping.
assumptions.fault_name: Duplicate ui_id accepted without reconciliation with bookkeeping

assumptions.statement: Requests arrive one at a time, so queue mutation needs no locking against concurrent start and install calls.
vulnerabilities: Race condition in queue mutation (concurrent start and install)

assumptions.statement: The deployment is a single-user local application, so authentication is unnecessary and absence of principals is acceptable.
assumptions.fault_name: No authentication surface anywhere on the manager routes
vulnerabilities: Information exposure of model inventory and fetched content

interface_agreements.statement: The client submits a model download as a JSON body to POST /manager/queue/install_model with keys name, url, filename, save_path and an optional ui_id; the /api prefix serves the same handler.

For a filename without a .safetensors suffix the handler requires the (name, save_path, filename) triple to exist in the default-channel model catalog and the url to equal a member of the catalog URL set exactly; a missing triple gives 400, a URL outside the set gives 403.
A filename ending in lowercase .safetensors bypasses catalog membership; any host-bearing URL is accepted with 200, while an uppercase .SAFETENSORS suffix is rejected with 400.
Status codes form the contract: 200 queued, 400 invalid request, 403 security denial, 500 unhandled exception; GET on install_model returns 404 and POST on status returns 405.
Accepted items do not process spontaneously; only GET /manager/queue/start drains the queue; the status counters are total_count, done_count, in_progress_count and is_processing.
The worker, not the request handler, performs the outbound fetch; the fetch happens after the enqueue response and follows the supplied URL scheme and authority.
The worker writes the fetched body to models/<save_path>/<filename>, creates missing directories, and concatenates the path components without canonicalization (a .. save_path is accepted).
A manager middleware enforces the model-install security policy ahead of the handler and answers 403 with the fixed message A security error has occurred.
The queue accepts a caller-supplied ui_id verbatim as arbitrary JSON; a dict value is accepted with 200 and processing then halts before the fetch.
GET /externalmodel/getlist?mode=default returns the catalog JSON with entries carrying name, type, base, save_path, description, reference, filename and url; the same catalog feeds the install gate.
Model inventory is exposed as JSON: /models lists directories, /experiment/models/<dir> lists files with size, created and modified; direct file GET paths return 404.
The worker processes queued items serially; one start drains every item unless processing halts; several items can be enqueued between starts.

trust_agreements.statement: The handler trusts the JSON body to encode a legitimate install request; no principal, session or token is read, and any anonymous client reaches the trust decision.

The gate trusts the validated catalog tuple and the queued tuple to be the same data; actually the catalogue lookup binds name, save_path and filename while the url is only checked for set membership across catalog URLs.
The gate trusts the filename suffix as the discriminator of scrutiny: lowercase .safetensors marks the item safe and skips catalog membership; the payload behind the name is never inspected.
The worker trusts the queued url to be a fetchable HTTP resource; the client is trusted not to aim the fetch at the internal network, the loopback interface or local files.
The worker trusts save_path and filename to be harmless path components under the models root; no canonicalization check runs before the write.
The write path trusts the fetched bytes to be a model payload; content is stored under the client-chosen name and every consumer of the model tree then trusts that name.
The queue trusts ui_id to be a hashable string; it is consumed in the progress and bookkeeping path without type validation.
The UI and operators trust the queue counters as authoritative execution truth; the reset path trusts done_count to mean completed work.
The manager trusts the fixed channel list (GitHub raw URLs, selected default) as the only catalog source; no runtime custom URL channel was observed.

The queue trusts state-changing operations (start, reset) to be deliberate; both are GET endpoints with no auth and no CSRF token, so any HTTP participant can cross the idle-to-drained and drained-to-stale transitions.

transitions.trigger: Further accepted installs before a start.
Install accepted on top of stale counters.
GET /manager/queue/start while the head item carries a non-string ui_id.
A further GET /manager/queue/start after the poison head is disposed.
GET start on an empty queue.
